answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof of costly history. Every identity must publish a signed ledger of prior work — a quill that only writes when real compute or capital has been burned — and peers counter-sign each entry. A newcomer cannot forge that chain without redoing the spend, so minting ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand times, not once. Rewards wait on a ledge above the pool: they unlock only after independent attestations, and identical fingerprints cancel each other. The opal of this design is scarcity of verifiable effort.
